$comment: Secret-shaped values in this repo's published history that are confirmed DEAD.
Keyed by SHA-256 so no secret is stored here. That costs nothing in safety:
every value listed is already in the published history in plaintext, which is
exactly why it needs listing. The digest identifies, it does not protect.
Why this file exists: scripts/audit-secrets.mjs scans git objects, so a value
that was ever committed is found forever, even after the credential is revoked.
Without this list the scanner fails on every run and the pre-push hook blocks
every push, which trains people to pass --no-verify by reflex. A scanner that is
always bypassed is worse than no scanner: it was a six-week blind spot on a live
service_role key that produced ROTATION.md 0.5 in the first place.
Allowlisted values are still PRINTED on every run with their reason and death
date. They stop failing the build; they do not stop being reported.
RULE: revoke first, then allowlist. Adding a live key here hides it permanently,
which is the one outcome this whole apparatus exists to prevent. 'Probably dead'
is not dead -- record how it was confirmed.
